name: 110 (One Hundred and Ten)
description: 110 (One Hundred and Ten) is an Irish trick-taking game with bidding, related to Twenty-Five. Played with a standard 52-card deck; the first player or team to reach 110 points wins. Players score 5 points per trick. Card ranking varies by trump suit.

overview.description: 110 (One Hundred and Ten) is an Irish trick-taking game with bidding, related to Twenty-Five. Played with a standard 52-card deck; the first player or team to reach 110 points wins. Players score 5 points per trick. Card ranking varies by trump suit.

history.origins: Ireland. Bidding version of the game Twenty-Five; part of the Irish trick-taking family (Twenty-Five, 55, 110, 220).
timeline: Early 2000s: modern rule summaries describe 110 as a bidding variant of the traditional Irish game Twenty-Five.

setup.players: 2–9 (five cards each plus five-card kitty from one 52-card pack)
setup.dealing: Five cards to each player and five to the kitty (two then three or three then two at a time); deal passes left.

rules.objective: Be the first player (or team) to reach 110 points. Each trick is worth 5 points; the holder of the highest trump in play gets an extra 5 points.
rules.gameplay: Bidding (10, 15, 20, 25, or 60) starts left of dealer; dealer may 'take' by equalling the bid. Highest bidder picks up the five-card kitty, discards five, and names trump (no robbing). Player to dealer's left leads; same card ranking as Twenty-Five (5 of trump highest, then J, then A of hearts).
keyRules: Bids: 10, 15, 20, 25, 60; dealer can take by equalling
Bidder takes kitty, discards 5, names trump
5 points per trick; +5 for highest trump in play

strategy.basic: Bid according to hand strength and trump potential; remember card ranking (5, J, A♥, then K-Q and numerals; red suits 'highest best', black 'lowest best'). The 5 of trump and J of trump are the top trumps; A of hearts is always trump.
strategy.intermediate: Competing with dealer: dealer can take by equalling, so bids can be pushed up. Holding the highest trump gives +5; time when you play it. In 110, reaching the target in the same deal—who took tricks first can decide the winner.
strategy.advanced: Bid 60 only when you can win all five tricks. If you bid lower and make all tricks you score 30 (five tricks + highest trump), not 60. Track who is close to 110 and whether to bid to win or to block.
tips: Same ranking as Twenty-Five: learn 5, J, A♥ as top trumps and red high / black low in non-trump.
Bidder names trump after taking kitty (or before, in some variants).
First to 110 wins; last hand is played out to see if bid succeeds.

variations.name: Only bidder can win
variations.description: Some groups play that only the bidder can win the game; if someone reaches 110 points through tricks taken against another player's bid, the game continues until the bidder wins or loses.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant changes only who is allowed to win the game and can be handled in scoring logic without separate engine overrides.

variations.name: Bidder names trump before kitty
variations.description: In some circles the bidder must name the trump suit before looking at the five-card kitty instead of naming trump after picking up and discarding.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes when trump is announced relative to the kitty and does not require a different engine structure here.

variations.name: Different first lead
variations.description: Some play that the first lead comes from the player to the left of the bidder; others play that the player to the right of the bidder leads the first trick instead.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation affects only which seat leads the first trick and can be expressed by table rules without dedicated override entries.

variations.name: Bidder scores only bid amount
variations.description: Some groups rule that the bidder can only score the amount bid; for example, a bid of 15 that wins all five tricks still scores 15 rather than 30.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant changes how much the bidder scores when exceeding their bid and is handled in scoring logic rather than separate engine overrides.

scoring.description: Bidder scores trick points if total ≥ bid, else loses the bid amount. Bid of 60 = win all tricks: score 60 or lose 60. Others score for their tricks. First to 110 wins; if two reach it in the same deal, order of tricks determines winner.
scoring.winCondition: Be the first player (or team) to reach 110 points. Each trick is worth 5 points; the holder of the highest trump in play gets an extra 5 points.
